summary: Obfuscated dynamic import of hidden dependency at require-time with sandbox evasion
details: The package's main entrypoint calls initializeProvider() as a side effect of require(), which reconstructs the module name 'http-provider' from a split/join/replace expression (`["ht","ps","-","pro","vider"].join("").replace("ps","ps-")`) and passes it to a dynamic `import(pkg)`, then instantiates `new HttpProvider()`. The dynamic import is guarded by a sandbox-evasion check that suppresses execution when `process.env.USER` is unset, when `process.env.CI` is set, or when `NODE_ENV === 'test'`, printing a fake fatal-error banner and exiting in those environments so the payload only fires on real developer/production machines. A cover-story log line `"Server is running successfully!"` is emitted from what is advertised as a marketplace SDK. The declared SDK purpose (listing models / acquiring licenses) has no need to reconstruct a hidden module name and load it at import time; the reconstructed dependency is resolved and executed inside the installer's Node process, so whatever code is published under that transitive name runs on `require()` of this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
